dedupe_keys.name: roskomnadzor register of communications licences russia with an aggregated open copy for 1991 to 2036

description: Roskomnadzor, the Russian federal regulator of communications, keeps the register of licences for communications services, which it publishes as open data. Each licence names the holder, the licensed service (for example local and long-distance telephony, mobile radiotelephone service, data transmission, telematic services or broadcasting), the territory, the issue date, status and expiry. An aggregated copy deposited on Harvard Dataverse in August 2026 by Roman P. Vasilev (KontragentPro) summarises all 195,993 licences issued since 1991, of which 20,519 are active, across 992 differently worded service types, in three tables: issues by year and status, distribution by service type, and expiry dates of active licences up to 2036. Coverage: the Russian Federation, 1991 to 2026, with expiries to 2036. Format and access: register files on the Roskomnadzor open data portal and CSV tables with a README (in Russian) on Dataverse, free of charge. Caveats: the Roskomnadzor site did not answer from this environment on 26 September 2026; the aggregate omits territories and holders; service names are not standardised; issues fell fivefold in 2024 and 2025 for reasons not explained. Simulation uses: market structure and the number of licensed operators by service, as context for telecom resilience and regulation studies. Related records: the ACMA register and FCC ULS are licence registers of other countries.
